name: Hermes CLI Commands
summary: Reusable command pack for local agent workflows and project tasks.
description: Hermes CLI Commands is a command-pack pattern for teams that want predictable local agent workflows. Instead of asking an agent to invent shell commands every time, you expose a small approved command surface for setup, test, lint, smoke checks, and release routines.
installSummary: This entry is a CLI command-pack pattern. Do not treat it as a universal public package install. Add command definitions to the agent or team CLI mechanism you actually use, then verify each command against the local project.

installSteps.title: Identify repeatable commands
installSteps.body: Start with commands the agent should run often and safely: install dependencies, run tests, run lint, start local server, smoke test, and collect logs.

installSteps.title: Create a command registry
installSteps.body: Put the commands in a visible file such as `agent-commands.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or your agent's command-pack format. Each command should include purpose, working directory, required environment, and expected output.

installSteps.title: Add safety notes
installSteps.body: Mark destructive commands as manual-only. The agent should never run reset, delete, deploy, or database migration commands without explicit user approval.

agentSetups.summary: Use Hermes' command or skill mechanism if available in your local setup; otherwise keep the command pack as project documentation.

steps.title: Command file
steps.body: Create a command file that Hermes can read before task execution. Keep names stable so prompts can reference them.

agentSetups.summary: Codex can use the same command pack when it is referenced in AGENTS.md or project docs.

steps.title: Document commands
steps.body: Add a section describing exact commands and when to run them.
steps.code:
## Project commands
- Install: `npm install`
- Check: `npm run astro check`
- Build: `npm run build`
- Preview: `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1`

agentSetups.summary: Claude Code users can put the same approved command list in CLAUDE.md.

steps.title: Add command policy
steps.body: Separate safe read/check commands from commands that require user confirmation.

primaryUseCases: Reduce repeated explanation of build, test, and local server commands.
Give agents a safe operating envelope inside a project.
Make onboarding smoother for projects with several agent users.
Convert tribal knowledge into reusable command documentation.
highlights: Improves reliability because agents reuse known commands instead of guessing.
Makes destructive or sensitive commands visibly gated.
Works as a lightweight bridge before building a full custom CLI.
Pairs with the Agent Setup Checklist for repeatable onboarding.

configuration.title: Command template
configuration.body: Use one template for each command so the agent can understand when and how to run it.
configuration.code:
### Command name
Purpose:
Run from:
Command:
Requires:
Expected success signal:
Do not run when:

verificationSteps.title: Run commands manually first
verificationSteps.body: Before telling an agent to use a command, run it yourself and record the expected successful output.

verificationSteps.title: Ask the agent to explain command choice
verificationSteps.body: For the first few runs, ask the agent to say which registered command it chose and why.

troubleshooting.title: Agent ignores command pack
troubleshooting.body: Move the command pack into the instruction file the agent always reads, or explicitly link it in the prompt.

troubleshooting.title: Command works for one developer only
troubleshooting.body: Replace machine-specific paths with project-relative commands and document required environment variables.

securityNotes: Never include secrets in command examples.
Mark deploy, delete, reset, migration, and production commands as approval-required.
limitations: This is a pattern, not a standardized public Hermes package.
The command pack needs manual upkeep when project scripts change.
Agents can still misuse commands if the trigger conditions are vague.
maintenanceNotes: Recheck the command pack whenever package scripts or local dev tooling changes.
Delete commands that are no longer safe or used.
requirements: A project with repeatable local commands
Agent instruction file or command-pack support
